# @ifc-lite/mcp

> A Model Context Protocol server for IFC models. Besides the model tools of ifc-lite, it carries the IfcSheet tools (names starting `ifcsheet_`): open an IFC, lay out a drawing set (plans, elevations, sections, schedules on numbered sheets), edit it, and issue it as PDF, DXF, a drawing register and a handover package. Runs over stdio (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor) or Streamable HTTP.

Start it with the folders it may read and write:

    npx @ifc-lite/mcp --allow /path/to/project

Every path an `ifcsheet_*` tool reads or writes must lie inside `--allow`. The tools never write an `.ifc` file or the model that was opened; the one exception is the annotated copy `ifcsheet_issue_set` writes as a new file when `annotated_ifc` is true. Details: README.md, section "Drawing sets (IfcSheet)".

## How a session works

- `ifcsheet_open_model` gives a `model_id`. The drawing-set tools keep their own handles; they do not need `model_load`.
- `ifcsheet_generate_set`, `ifcsheet_apply_template` and `ifcsheet_load_project` each make a drawing set and give a `document_id`. The editing tools change that set in the session's memory; the PDF, DXF and issue always draw the latest edit. Nothing is on disk until `ifcsheet_save_project` or an export.
- Lengths are metres in the viewer frame (X east, Y up, Z south). Paper sizes are millimetres. A scale is its denominator: 100 means 1:100.
- `dry_run: true` on `ifcsheet_add_view`, `ifcsheet_place_view`, `ifcsheet_set_title_block`, `ifcsheet_add_schedule`, `ifcsheet_apply_template` and `ifcsheet_renumber` reports what the call would change and changes nothing. Ids a dry run reports are not kept.
- `ifcsheet_undo` takes back the last edit of a set and `ifcsheet_redo` re-applies it. Dry runs are not in the history; a new edit after an undo clears redo; the last 50 edits are kept. Undo with nothing to undo says so and is not an error. `ifcsheet_save_project` still writes the set to disk.

## Tools

- `ifcsheet_open_model`: parse an IFC (`file_path` or `ifc_base64`); returns `model_id`, storeys with elevations, counts and the building's extent.
- `ifcsheet_check_readiness`: what the model lacks that the drawings read (storeys, rooms, materials, quantities, unique GlobalIds); `ready` and the findings.
- `ifcsheet_generate_set`: the default set (a plan per storey, elevations, proposed sections); returns `document_id`, sheets, views.
- `ifcsheet_apply_template`: lay the set out by a `.bvset` template; returns a new `document_id` and the notes of what its rules met.
- `ifcsheet_load_project`: a set from a saved `.ifclite-project.json` on an opened model.
- `ifcsheet_list_sheets`: the sheets (number, name, paper, views with slot and scale), the views not placed, the title block fields.
- `ifcsheet_add_view`: add a plan (by `level`), elevation (by `direction`), section (by `axis` and `offset_m`, or a line `from`/`to`) or axonometric (by `preset`, optionally cut away); not on a sheet until placed.
- `ifcsheet_place_view`: put a view on a sheet at a scale; without `sheet` the engine's rule chooses or makes one; errors when the views do not fit.
- `ifcsheet_set_title_block`: set title block fields, project-wide or for one sheet (client, drawnBy, checkedBy, date, phase, projectNumber, projectManager, designer, address...); returns the fields in force and the ones that changed.
- `ifcsheet_renumber`: renumber the sheets by a scheme (`default` A-101 style, `sequential` A01, A02...).
- `ifcsheet_add_schedule`: a room and area schedule (`rooms`, with the building total Au as `total_row`) a bill of quantities (`boq`, from a saved project's articles) or a table from the Lists engine (`list`, with a definition of columns, grouping and sums; the same rows and totals as the app's Lists panel) on a sheet of its own.
- `ifcsheet_export_pdf`: the set as one PDF, a page per sheet at true scale.
- `ifcsheet_export_dxf`: one DXF per sheet into a directory.
- `ifcsheet_issue_set`: the PDF, a DXF per sheet, `register.csv`, the schedules as CSV and, with `handover: true`, `handover.zip` (with the IFC as opened); `annotated_ifc: true` adds the annotated copy of the IFC.
- `ifcsheet_save_project`: write the set as `.ifclite-project.json`; what a loaded file held besides the set is written back unchanged.
- `ifcsheet_undo`: take back the last edit of a set (add_view, place_view, set_title_block, add_schedule, renumber); `changed` is false when there is nothing to undo.
- `ifcsheet_redo`: re-apply the edit just undone; a new edit clears it.

## Resources

- `ifcsheet://project/schema`: the JSON Schema of the project document the tools save and load.
- `ifcsheet://session/project`: the project document of the set the session made or loaded last, as `ifcsheet_save_project` would write it. Read-only; listed once the session holds a set.
- `ifcsheet://session/sheets`: the sheets of that set, as `ifcsheet_list_sheets` returns them. Read-only.

## Prompts

- `prepare_permit_set`: open, lay out, title block, room schedule and Au, readiness, save, issue with handover (arguments: `model_path`, `output_dir`, and optionally the title block fields).
- `update_set_for_new_model`: open a new model version, load the saved project on it, add plans for storeys that have none, check readiness, issue again.
- `check_readiness_and_fix`: check readiness and say what only the model's author can fix.

## Limits

- The DXF files hold lines and no text.
- The plain title block of the PDF prints the project, the sheet number and name, the scale and the date. The other title block fields are kept in the project for the app's title block layouts.
- A schedule's rows are read from the model each time the set is drawn. Rows beyond what fits the sheet's paper are left off the drawn sheet (`rows_left_off` says how many); the CSV of the issue has all of them.
- `annotated_ifc` writes no annotations: dimensions, tags and notes are drafts of the app, and these tools hold none. The result says so.
- A session keeps at most 8 opened models in memory; the oldest is dropped, with its sets.

## Hosted endpoint (opt-in)

The web app can serve the drawing-set tools over Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`. It is OFF unless the deployment sets the environment variable `IFCSHEET_HOSTED_MCP=1`; without it the endpoint answers 404 and nothing else changes.

- POST only, JSON in and JSON out (a single message or a batch). No server-side sessions, no resources, no prompts, no server-initiated stream: every request starts from nothing unless it carries a session token (below), and a batch (at most 20 messages) shares one state and runs its messages one after the other, in order, so `ifcsheet_open_model` then a tool taking its `model_id` works inside one batch: the ids are sequential within a request (`sheetmodel-1`, `sheetmodel-2`, ...), so the first model a batch opens is `sheetmodel-1`. Across requests only a session token carries a project over. A body that is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 message is answered with -32600 (Invalid Request), invalid JSON with -32700.
- Only the `ifcsheet_*` tools. The server has no file system for you: every file path (`file_path`, `*_path`, `directory`) is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED. Send the model as `ifc_base64`, a template or project as `template_json` or `project_json`, and read results from the response (`ifcsheet_export_pdf` without `file_path` returns `pdf_base64`). `ifcsheet_generate_set` takes `ifc_base64` directly, so one call turns a model into a set.
- Nothing is saved on the server: edits are returned in the response, never stored.
- Sessions (opt-in, client-held). The server keeps nothing between requests, because serverless instances do not share memory. Set `IFCSHEET_HOSTED_MCP_SECRET` (32 characters or more) and every tool takes an optional `session_token` and returns a fresh one in `structuredContent.session_token`: the project built so far (the sets and their schedules, gzip, base64url) and a SHA-256 reference to each model, signed with HMAC-SHA-256 and valid for an hour from the call that issued it (`session_expires_at`). Send it back on the next call. A model is too big to carry, so a call that names a `model_id` or `document_id` also sends the same file as `ifc_base64`; the server checks it against the hash in the token and parses it again unless this instance already holds it (a cache of 2 models / about 200 MB, least recently used out first). A changed, foreign or expired token, a missing model and different bytes are each answered with an error result saying what to do. One request carries one session (a batch must send the same token), a session names at most 8 models, a token is at most 1 MiB, and undo history is not carried. A token is a bearer value: anyone holding it can replay that project state until it expires. It holds no path and grants no file access, and nothing of a token or a model is logged. Without the secret the endpoint stays stateless and the tools take no `session_token`.
- Limits: a model of at most 25 MB (larger is refused with an error result), a request body to match, and 50 seconds per request (stopped with HTTP 504 and a JSON-RPC error). The 50 s limit is checked between messages and answered when it passes, but it cannot interrupt a synchronous parse or layout already running: such a call runs to its end (the platform's own function limit is then the stop). The hosting platform may set a smaller body limit than 25 MB (Vercel: 4.5 MB), which then applies first.

## Example session

A user asks: "Open /work/AC20-FZK-Haus.ifc and issue a drawing set into /work/issue, with the room schedule."

1. `ifcsheet_open_model` `{"file_path": "/work/AC20-FZK-Haus.ifc"}` returns `model_id: "sheetmodel-1"`, project 'Projekt-FZK-Haus', storeys Erdgeschoss (0) and Dachgeschoss (2.7 m).
2. `ifcsheet_check_readiness` `{"model_id": "sheetmodel-1"}` returns `ready: false` with one finding, `noMaterials`: 4 of 82 elements have no material.
3. `ifcsheet_generate_set` `{"model_id": "sheetmodel-1"}` returns `document_id: "sheetset-1"` with sheets A-101, A-201, A-202 and A-301 and 9 views.
4. `ifcsheet_set_title_block` `{"document_id": "sheetset-1", "fields": {"phase": "DTAC", "projectNumber": "42/2026"}, "dry_run": true}` reports the two fields it would set. The same call without `dry_run` sets them.
5. `ifcsheet_add_schedule` `{"document_id": "sheetset-1", "kind": "rooms", "locale": "ro"}` adds sheet A-601 and returns the table and `total_row`, the building total (Au).
6. `ifcsheet_save_project` `{"document_id": "sheetset-1", "file_path": "/work/issue/fzk.ifclite-project.json"}` writes the project.
7. `ifcsheet_issue_set` `{"document_id": "sheetset-1", "directory": "/work/issue", "handover": true}` writes the PDF, five DXF files, `register.csv`, `schedules/A-601.csv` and `handover.zip`, and lists them with their sizes.

To resume later: open the new or same IFC, then `ifcsheet_load_project` with the saved file.
